📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1107 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Why obesity affects men and women differently may be hiding in their fat

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1107 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Scientists at the University of California, Riverside have uncovered a surprising difference in how the immune systems of males and females respond to obesity.
  • Recent findings suggest that the discovery centers on eosinophils, immune cells best known for their involvement in allergies and asthma.
  • It has been revealed that the study, published in PNAS Nexus, was led by University of California, Riverside biomedical scientists Meera Nair and Adam Godzik.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scientists at the University of California, Riverside have uncovered a surprising difference in how the immune systems of males and females respond to obesity. Their findings suggest that certain immune cells found in body fat can help protect against inflammation and metabolic problems, while others may make these harmful effects worse.

Recent findings suggest that the discovery centers on eosinophils, immune cells best known for their involvement in allergies and asthma. In experiments with mice, researchers found that these cells behave differently depending on biological sex, potentially helping explain why obesity does not affect males and females in the same way.

It has been revealed that the study, published in PNAS Nexus, was led by University of California, Riverside biomedical scientists Meera Nair and Adam Godzik. Their findings challenge the longstanding assumption that eosinophils are largely similar cells with relatively few specialized functions. The results also point toward potential upcoming approaches for treating obesity and its complications.

Six Types of Immune Cells Found in Body Fat.

Sources indicate that to investigate the role of eosinophils in obesity, the researchers used high-resolution single-cell sequencing, a technique that allows scientists to examine gene activity in individual cells. They identified six distinct eosinophil populations in adipose (fat) tissue, each with its own pattern of gene expression and potentially different biological functions.

This unexpected diversity suggests that eosinophils play a much more complicated role in metabolic health than previously recognized.

"Eosinophils are more complex than we once thought," remarked Nair, a professor of biomedical sciences in the UCR School of Medicine. "Some populations can protect against obesity, and if we can identify and activate the pathways that produce these protective cells, we may find new ways to improve metabolic health.".

Why Male and Female Fat Tissue Respond Differently.

One of the most striking discoveries was a difference in the immune cells found in male and female mice.

Female mice possessed a protective population of eosinophils that appeared to communicate more effectively with macrophages, another group of immune cells present in fat tissue. According to Nair, this cooperation may help create a healthier environment within fat tissue and support better metabolic function.

It has been revealed that male mice indicated a different pattern. When given a diet high in fat, they were more likely to develop eosinophil populations associated with inflammation. Their fat tissue also contained eosinophils with gene activity patterns suggesting weaker protective functions.

Industry observers note that these findings indicate that the effects of eosinophils on obesity depend on more than simply how many of these cells are present. The particular type of eosinophil and its interactions with neighboring immune cells may be equally vital.

Industry observers note that "This means the relationship between eosinophils and obesity is not simply a matter of how many eosinophils are present," said Rebecca E. Ruggiero-Ruff, a postdoctoral researcher in Nair's lab and co-first author of the paper. "Their functional characteristics and how they communicate with other immune cells are also critical.".

A Protein That May Help Protect Against Inflammation.

The researchers also identified a protein called RELM alpha that appears to play an important role in maintaining the beneficial relationship between eosinophils and macrophages.

Industry observers note that produced by macrophages, RELM alpha seemed to help stabilize communication between the two immune cell types in female mice. This interaction may be one reason certain eosinophil populations are better able to support healthy fat tissue.

According to recent reports, the finding builds on earlier experiments by the same research group, which highlighted that administering RELM alpha to mice produced protective effects. Together, the results suggest that the protein may help regulate immune activity within fat tissue and influence how the body responds to obesity.

Could the Discovery Lead to Better Obesity Treatments?

In a recent development, although the results offer newly introduced insight into the biology of obesity, the experiments were conducted in mice. Researchers have also detected eosinophils in fat tissue from people with obesity, but scientists do not yet fully understand what these cells do in the human body.

Nair cautioned that additional research will be necessary before the discovery can be used to develop treatments. One particularly vital question is whether therapies targeting the immune system would work differently in men and women.

"A drug may not activate the same pathways or produce the same effects in males and females, particularly when it targets the immune system," remarked co-first author Xinru Qiu, a postdoctoral researcher in Godzik's lab. "We need to investigate sex-specific biology more thoroughly so that treatments can be optimized for different patients.".

Understanding these differences could eventually help researchers design more personalized treatments for obesity and the metabolic complications associated with it.

Scientists Strategy to Recreate Human Fat Tissue in the Lab.

The research team is now investigating whether the protective behavior observed in mouse eosinophils can also be studied in human laboratory models.

According to recent reports, to accomplish this, the scientists are developing three-dimensional adipose organoids. These miniature laboratory models reproduce certain features of real fat tissue, allowing researchers to examine how eosinophils interact with fat cells and other components of their environment.

The goal is to determine whether changing communication between immune cells could encourage healthier responses in human fat tissue.

"We ultimately hope to develop human adipose organoids that will allow us to investigate whether manipulating immune-cell communication can promote healthier tissue responses," remarked Godzik, a professor of biomedical sciences and the Bruce D. and Nancy B. Varner Presidential Endowed Chair in Cancer Research.

The findings raise the possibility that targeting specific immune cell populations, rather than treating all eosinophils as functionally identical, could eventually provide new ways to address obesity and its complications. Whether the same protective mechanisms operate in humans remains an important question for future research.

The research team also included Lauren Vance, Yuxin He, and Djurdjica Coss, who worked alongside Nair, Godzik, Ruggiero-Ruff, and Qiu.

Funding for the study came from the National Institutes of Health, the UCR School of Medicine, and the California Institute for Regenerative Medicine.

The research paper is titled "Single-cell heterogeneity of adipose eosinophils is shaped by sex and RELMα and linked to macrophage communication networks in obesity.".

  • The credit bureau has moved nearly all of its on-premises data centers to the cloud and runs workloads across Amazon Web Services Inc., Google LLC’s Google Cloud and Oracle Corp.’s cloud infrastructure, according to Avinash Singh (pictured), vice president of technology services at Equifax.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 15:53 EST / NOVEMBER 20 2026.

A multicloud strategy once meant deciding which workloads lived with which provider. Now database providers are moving into the clouds customers already use, and AI projects are raising the value of those migrations well beyond the back office.

Equifax Inc. is a case in point. The credit bureau has moved nearly all of its on-premises data centers to the cloud and runs workloads across Amazon Web Services Inc., Google LLC’s Google Cloud and Oracle Corp.’s cloud infrastructure, according to Avinash Singh (pictured), vice president of technology services at Equifax.

Recent findings suggest that “Their performance optimizer is so advanced that we don’t need to tune a single query,” Singh said. “Just think about that. Fifteen to 20 tickets per day turns into one to two tickets per month.”.

Singh spoke with theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante at Oracle AI World, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how a multicloud strategy is helping Equifax cut billing database tickets. (* Disclosure below.).

Equifax’s global billing system runs on Oracle’s billing and revenue management software, rating and invoicing billions of transactions each month. The database behind it ran on Amazon Relational Database Service for Oracle until it hit a 65-terabyte ceiling. Oracle Autonomous AI Database on AWS, built on Exadata hardware, has room for petabytes of data inside the same cloud, as enterprise adoption accelerates. Because the application stack stayed on AWS, only the database service changed, Singh explained.

Sources indicate that “There is zero code writing because it is just about migrating the data from one database to another,” Singh said. “We achieved this migration without any downtime.”.

According to recent reports, the results demonstrated up quickly after the system went live in April. Gathering database statistics on nearly 100 terabytes of data dropped from three to four days to three to four hours. After some configuration tuning, batch jobs that once handled 100 to 200 rows per transaction now process 15,000 to 30,000, according to Singh.

In a recent development, “Our rating improved almost 200% to 300%,” Singh stated. “We are able to close our books way before what we have been closing.”.

Breaking: Scientists discover a hidden hereditary form of aggressive prostate cancer

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1068 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that scientists have identified a previously unrecognized inherited form of prostate cancer that, although extremely rare, can lead to aggressive disease relatively early in life.
  • It has been revealed that most cancers develop as genetic changes build up in cells over time.
  • In a recent development, among the most familiar examples are mutations in the BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that scientists have identified a previously unrecognized inherited form of prostate cancer that, although extremely rare, can lead to aggressive disease relatively early in life. The discovery, made by researchers at the University of British Columbia (UBC), could help doctors identify families with a heightened genetic risk and detect cancer before it spreads.

It has been revealed that most cancers develop as genetic changes build up in cells over time. However, approximately 5% to 10% are associated with inherited mutations that can be passed from parents to their children, creating a cancer risk that may extend across generations.

In a recent development, among the most familiar examples are mutations in the BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes. These inherited changes can substantially raise the likelihood of breast, ovarian, pancreatic, and prostate cancers. Testing for BRCA mutations has reshaped cancer prevention and treatment by allowing people with elevated risks to receive earlier screening and preventive care.

In a recent development, now, a study published in Cancer Discovery points to another gene, CDK12, as a potentially crucial marker of inherited prostate cancer risk. After examining genetic information from more than 4,500 people with aggressive prostate cancer, the researchers discovered five unrelated men with inherited mutations in CDK12. Every one of these men developed metastatic prostate cancer between ages 44 and 62, meaning the cancer had spread beyond the prostate.

Recent findings suggest that "What's striking is that every patient we identified with this inherited mutation had already developed metastatic disease by the time they were diagnosed," remarked senior author Dr. Alexander Wyatt, associate professor of urologic sciences in the UBC faculty of medicine and UBC President's Excellence Chair in Precision Oncology. "The opportunity now is to identify these families earlier and give people the chance to benefit from enhanced screening, when there are still curative treatment options.".

A Hidden Genetic Cause of Aggressive Prostate Cancer.

Recent findings suggest that the discovery challenges a longstanding assumption about CDK12. Scientists previously believed that harmful changes in this gene developed spontaneously inside cancer cells rather than being inherited from a parent.

To investigate whether the inherited mutations were actually contributing to the disease, the team examined the patients' tumors for a distinctive pattern of genetic damage associated with loss of CDK12 function. This molecular fingerprint helped connect the inherited mutations to the development of their cancers.

Sources indicate that "The tumors provided us with a genetic signature that pointed directly back to CDK12," mentioned lead author Dr. Sofie Tolmeijer, a postdoctoral fellow in the Wyatt lab. "It gave us compelling evidence that these inherited mutations were playing a direct role in causing their cancer.".

The findings emerged from a broad international research effort involving UBC, BC Cancer, the Vancouver Coastal Health Research Institute, and the University of Washington, along with scientists at institutions in Australia, the Netherlands, Spain, and Belgium.

Despite the potentially serious consequences, inherited CDK12 mutations appear to be exceptionally uncommon. The researchers found them in approximately one out of every 1,000 people with aggressive prostate cancer. Even at that low frequency, they estimate that hundreds of families around the world could be affected.

It has been revealed that "While this mutation is extremely rare, the discovery could be lifesaving for the families who carry it," said Dr. Tolmeijer. "Finding one person with an inherited mutation gives us the opportunity to identify other family members at risk and help them take action before cancer develops or spreads.".

Genetic Testing Could Help Detect Prostate Cancer Earlier.

One of the most promising implications of the discovery is that doctors may not need to develop entirely upcoming testing technology to put the findings into practice.

The researchers recommend including CDK12 in standard genetic testing panels used to assess hereditary prostate cancer risk. These panels examine multiple genes associated with inherited cancer susceptibility, helping identify individuals who may benefit from closer medical monitoring.

In a recent development, importantly, the clinical technology required to detect CDK12 mutations already exists. That could make expanding genetic testing relatively straightforward, potentially reducing the time and expense needed to bring the discovery into routine patient care.

"One of the most exciting aspects of this discovery is that we already have the technology needed to act on it," noted Dr. Wyatt, who is also a senior research scientist at the Vancouver Prostate Centre and senior scientist at BC Cancer. "Adding CDK12 to existing genetic tests is relatively straightforward, which means this discovery could move from the research lab into clinical care much more rapidly.".

Could the Same Mutation Increase Ovarian Cancer Risk?

The study also uncovered clues suggesting that inherited CDK12 mutations might be associated with ovarian cancer, although more research is needed to establish whether they increase the risk.

Industry observers note that several of the men with inherited CDK12 mutations had relatives with a history of ovarian cancer. The investigators also identified another person who had ovarian cancer and carried an inherited CDK12 mutation. Analysis of that person's tumor revealed the same characteristic genetic signature seen in the prostate cancer cases.

Together, these observations suggest that CDK12 could potentially play a role in hereditary cancer risk beyond the prostate. Further studies will be needed to determine how strongly the mutations are associated with ovarian cancer and whether they should influence screening recommendations.

For families carrying these rare mutations, the potential benefits of identifying their genetic risk could be substantial. Earlier testing may give relatives the opportunity to receive closer surveillance and, if cancer develops, begin treatment before it reaches an advanced stage.

"With the right genetic testing and screening programs, we envision a future where no one who inherits one of these mutations dies from cancer," remarked Dr. Wyatt.

The research received funding from the Prostate Cancer Foundation, Terry Fox Research Institute, Canadian Cancer Society, Canadian Institutes of Health Research, Michael Smith Health Research BC, U.S. National Institutes of Health, BC Cancer Foundation, and other funding partners.

Upcoming Homes Are Now $40K Cheaper Than Existing Homes

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Upcoming-construction homes are less expensive than existing ones, and the difference has never been larger, the National Association of Home Builders has found.
  • Recent findings suggest that last month's NAHB/Wells Fargo Cost of Housing Index found the median new-home price is $393,300, compared to a median-priced existing home, which comes to $432,900 in the third quarter of 2026.
  • Builders, struggling to find buyers, are digging deeper to offer incentives on new homes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Upcoming-construction homes are less expensive than existing ones, and the difference has never been larger, the National Association of Home Builders has found.

Recent findings suggest that last month's NAHB/Wells Fargo Cost of Housing Index found the median new-home price is $393,300, compared to a median-priced existing home, which comes to $432,900 in the third quarter of 2026. That's the largest difference between new- and existing-home prices in the history of NAHB's tracking, Chairman Bill Owens said.

Builders, struggling to find buyers, are digging deeper to offer incentives on new homes. The National Association of Home Builders/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index plunged to a 14-year low last week. Many of the nation's major homebuilders have reported large year-over-year declines in revenue. But housing starts continue apace, showing some hope for the market long term.

“Builders are working with buyers to make new homes more affordable and appealing in a tough market, yet the latest CHI data show housing costs still overburden families,” NAHB Chief Economist Robert Dietz remarked in a statement.

A typical family would have to pay 36% of their income for a median-priced existing home. They'd need 33% of their income for a new home, a drop of 1% from the second quarter. And that accounts for a $17,000 drop in the median new-home price in the second quarter, when it was $434,900, NAHB found.

“As builders contend with rising construction costs, tighter lending standards and persistent labor shortages, policymakers should remove regulatory obstacles, enact permitting reform and create a stronger business environment that enables builders to produce more attainable, affordable homes,” Dietz said.

Industry observers note that housing costs across the board are rising. Owners are also struggling to manage insurance costs, HOA fees, and utilities.

In a recent development, NAHB's data indicates that the San Jose, CA, area is the most cost-burdened market in the third quarter, and 79% of a typical family's income is needed to make a mortgage payment on an existing home. Honolulu, San Diego, San Fransisco, and Barnstable Town, MA, follow. All are above 60%.

Meanwhile, the least cost-burdened market is Decatur, IL, where 17% of a typical family's income is needed to make a mortgage payment on an existing home. Elmira, NY, Peoria, IL, Wichita Falls, TX, and Springfield, IL, all also sit under 20%.

According to recent reports, NAHB studied 175 markets and found that, in 95 of them, the typical family is cost-burdened, meaning they spend more than 31% of their income on a median-priced existing home. Eight of those markets are severely cost-burdened, where they pay more than 50%.

It has been revealed that owens stated that price cuts and incentives are improving affordability. But the nation needs more pro-building laws to solve the underlying problem.

"According to our latest survey, 43% cut prices in October—the highest share since 2020—and 65% offered sales incentives," Owens stated. "But policymakers must do more to reduce red tape, address labor shortages, and fix supply chains so builders can expand the nation’s housing supply.”.

Part of the story is that it's a rough housing market all around.

The average rate on 30-year fixed home loans jumped to 7.28% last week, up from 7.11% recorded the week before and 6.26% last year, according to Freddie Mac. Pending home sales fell to a record low in October, and existing-home sales hit their lowest level since 2010.

Recent findings suggest that but part of the story is also how builders have changed up their business. The latest Realtor.com® quarterly construction insights report finds that existing homes are more expensive than new ones based on the price per square foot: $218 for new homes, $219 for existing ones.

Realtor.com senior economist Joel Berner writes that this month's latest-construction data points to builders expecting tough conditions to continue.

"Builders are dealing with a litany of obstacles to selling homes, whether it’s rising costs of land, labor, and materials, high financing costs, or weak buyer demand," Berner states. "This month’s data shows them slowing down activity at the top of their funnel, which will result in slower months of starts and completions later on.".

  • In a recent development, the headline is the first element of your Facebook ad copy that users will see.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in the digital age, social media platforms have become powerful tools for real estate agents to market their listings and attract potential clients. Among the various platforms available, Facebook remains a dominant force with its massive user base and advertising capabilities. To stand out in the competitive real estate market, agents must not only create compelling visual content but also craft persuasive ad copy that engages and captivates their target audience. In this article, we will delve into the key elements and strategies for writing effective Facebook ad copy, equipping real estate agents with the knowledge to maximize their advertising efforts and generate leads.

The first step to writing compelling Facebook ad copy is gaining a deep understanding of your target audience. By knowing their demographics, preferences, and pain points, you can tailor your copy to resonate with their needs and desires. Conduct thorough market research, utilize Facebook's audience insights, and analyze data from previous campaigns to gather valuable information about your target audience.

In a recent development, the headline is the first element of your Facebook ad copy that users will see. It needs to be attention-grabbing and compelling enough to entice people to read further. Use action-oriented words, emphasize unique selling propositions, and create a sense of urgency to pique the audience's curiosity and encourage them to click on your ad.

According to recent reports, when writing Facebook ad copy, it's crucial to highlight the benefits of the property or service you're promoting, rather than merely listing its features. Benefits explain how the property or service can improve the lives of potential buyers or renters. By emphasizing the value and advantages, you can create an emotional connection with your audience and motivate them to take action.

Recent findings suggest that storytelling is a powerful tool for capturing the attention of your audience and making your Facebook ad copy more relatable. Craft a compelling narrative that showcases the unique aspects of the property or the positive experiences of previous clients. Engaging stories can evoke emotions, create a sense of authenticity, and build trust with potential clients.

In the fast-paced world of social media, attention spans are limited. To ensure your Facebook ad copy is effective, keep it concise and clear. Use short sentences and paragraphs, bullet points, and subheadings to enhance readability. Avoid jargon and technical terms that may confuse or alienate your audience.

Industry observers note that social proof, such as testimonials, reviews, or success stories, can significantly influence potential clients' decision-making process. Incorporate social proof into your Facebook ad copy to build credibility and trust. Highlight positive feedback from satisfied clients or showcase awards and recognition you've received in the real estate industry.

Recent findings suggest that to encourage immediate action from your audience, create a sense of urgency in your Facebook ad copy. Limited-time offers exclusive deals, or a countdown timer can instill a fear of missing out (FOMO) and prompt potential clients to take the desired action promptly.

It has been revealed that an effective call-to-action (CTA) is vital to prompt users to take the desired action, whether it's contacting you, visiting a landing page, or scheduling a property viewing. Use action verbs, provide clear instructions, and create a sense of urgency to motivate users to click on your CTA button.

Continuous testing and optimization are essential for improving the performance of your Facebook ad copy. Create multiple variations of your ad copy, test them against each other, and analyze the results. Fine-tune your copy based on metrics such as click-through rates (CTR), conversion rates, and engagement levels to identify what resonates best with your audience.

Writing compelling Facebook ad copy is a crucial skill for real estate agents looking to excel in their digital marketing efforts. By understanding their target audience, crafting attention-grabbing headlines, focusing on benefits, incorporating storytelling techniques, and utilizing social proof, agents can create persuasive and engaging copy that captivates potential clients. Remember to keep your copy concise and clear, create a sense of urgency, and use compelling calls to action. Through A/B testing and continuous optimization, agents can refine their ad copy to maximize its effectiveness. By mastering the art of writing Facebook ad copy, real estate agents can unlock the full potential of social media advertising and boost their success in the competitive real estate market.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 16:28 EST / NOVEMBER 20 2026.

An Anthropic PBC researcher claims to have used Claude to prove the Riemann hypothesis, which is widely considered to be the most key open question in mathematics.

It has been revealed that levent Alpöge revealed his discovery today on his personal website. Anthropic has not published an official announcement about the news. The company floated on the Nasdaq a day earlier in a landmark public offering that raised over $93 billion.

It has been revealed that “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann hypothesis,” Alpöge wrote in a four-page statement. “What I saw during the course of progress so amazed me that I believe it is one dawn across science of something far greater.”.

The Riemann hypothesis was proposed in the mid-1800s by its namesake, the mathematician Bernhard Riemann. It focuses on a specific mathematical function, the Riemann zeta function, that was discovered more than a century earlier. A function is similar to a software program: It takes a piece of data as input and outputs another piece of data. A function’s input and output can be numbers, other functions and many other mathematical objects.

In a recent development, the Riemann zeta function’s input and output are both complex numbers. Complex numbers share similarities with regular numbers, but also have many additional properties. When the inputs and outputs of the Riemann zeta function are visualized, they resemble a three-dimensional spiral.

According to recent reports, the Riemann hypothesis is concerned with a specific section of that 3D spiral. In that section, the complex numbers outputted by the Riemann zeta function all equal zero. The hypothesis argues that the inputs from which those outputs are derived all include the value ½.

It has been revealed that the hypothesis is considered to be the most important open problem in mathematics for multiple reasons. The first is that although it focuses on a single, not overly complicated mathematical function, its implications extend to a far bigger topic: prime numbers. If the Riemann hypothesis is correct, a seemingly random aspect of prime numbers is in fact regulated by a pattern.

Another factor behind the hypothesis’ importance is that hundreds of theorems operate on the assumption that it’s true. If the Riemann hypothesis is correct, those theorems are correct as well.

Alpöge wrote that Claude proved not only the standard version of the Riemann hypothesis but also the so-called generalized variant. The latter conjecture argues that the Riemann hypothesis holds true for not only the Riemann zeta function but also certain other, similar functions. Alpöge believes that Claude will be capable of proving an even broader version of the hypothesis in the future.

Recent findings suggest that the researcher detailed that Claude’s proof runs for more than 250,000 pages. He has not yet released the paper. He did, however, publish a version of the proof written in Lean, a programming language used to verify mathematical results. The file contains millions of lines of code.

Industry observers note that proofs implemented in Lean are essentially regular software programs. If a Lean program runs without crashing, the mathematical argument that it describes is correct. That makes it easier for mathematicians to verify newly published proofs.

A rare disease reveals a hidden flaw in the immune system

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1160 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For decades, scientists believed they understood what caused the dangerous inflammation associated with a rare genetic disorder.
  • Recent findings suggest that the condition, known as mevalonate kinase deficiency (MKD), can cause severe inflammatory episodes that are sometimes life-threatening.
  • Industry observers note that the researchers found that these cells malfunction in people with MKD, setting off an excessive inflammatory response when infections occur.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For decades, scientists believed they understood what caused the dangerous inflammation associated with a rare genetic disorder. Now, researchers at the Garvan Institute of Medical Research have uncovered evidence that challenges 30 years of established thinking and could open the door to a latest treatment.

Recent findings suggest that the condition, known as mevalonate kinase deficiency (MKD), can cause severe inflammatory episodes that are sometimes life-threatening. A latest study published in Immunity identifies a previously underrecognized problem involving natural killer (NK) cells, immune cells that normally help the body eliminate infected cells.

Industry observers note that the researchers found that these cells malfunction in people with MKD, setting off an excessive inflammatory response when infections occur. The discovery also points to a possible treatment using existing medications called JAK inhibitors, which could be particularly valuable for patients who do not respond to current therapies.

Sources indicate that "This study has revealed a upcoming target for this inflammatory disorder and sets the scene for future clinical studies to explore the use of JAK inhibitors or other drugs to neutralize interferon gamma in patients with MKD," indicates Professor Mike Rogers, Lab Head at Garvan and senior author of the study. "This could lead to a targeted treatment that hasn't been tried before.".

Why a Rare Immune Disease Causes Dangerous Inflammation.

According to recent reports, MKD is a lifelong condition known to affect hundreds of children and adults around the world, although researchers suspect that many people with the disorder have never been diagnosed. Patients experience recurring attacks of high fever, skin rashes, joint pain, and inflammation in the abdomen. The most serious episodes can cause potentially fatal complications.

For roughly three decades, research into the disease has largely centered on macrophages, immune cells that help coordinate the body's inflammatory defenses. Existing treatments are designed to block an inflammatory signal released by these cells. However, approximately half of patients do not respond adequately, leaving a major need for better treatment options.

To investigate what might be missing from the prevailing explanation, the Garvan team examined blood samples from people with MKD and studied preclinical models of the disorder.

Industry observers note that their experiments revealed a significant defect in natural killer cells, which play an important role in the body's early defenses against viral infections. In MKD, these cells fail to mature properly and struggle to perform one of their most important functions: destroying infected cells before an infection can spread.

The consequences go beyond an impaired ability to fight infection. When natural killer cells cannot eliminate their targets, they release large amounts of inflammatory signaling molecules, activating other parts of the immune system and potentially triggering widespread inflammation.

Recent findings suggest that "We found that these immune cells are essentially misfiring," explains Professor Rogers. "NK cells are loaded with toxic ammunition, stored in granules that are released to kill infected cells. However, in MKD these toxic granules can't be released from NK cells and remain trapped inside. When an NK cell fails to kill its target, it compensates by shouting for help, pumping out large amounts of interferon gamma - a powerful inflammatory signal. This activates other immune cells and causes the dangerous fever and widespread inflammation seen in patients.".

Discovery Challenges 30 Years of Immune Disease Research.

The findings suggest that natural killer cell dysfunction, rather than macrophage activity alone, plays a central role in driving MKD.

Dr. Marcia Munoz, Group Leader in the Rogers Lab and lead researcher on the study, states the results represent a major change in how scientists understand the disease.

It has been revealed that "This really turns on its head 30 years of dogma about what was thought to be the underlying mechanism of disease. In MKD, the primary problem is in NK cells and not in macrophages, as previously believed," she says.

To investigate how this cellular defect contributes to the disorder, the Garvan researchers collaborated with Professor Mariapia Degli-Esposti and scientists at Monash University.

It has been revealed that using preclinical models, the team established a connection between malfunctioning natural killer cells and the severe symptoms associated with MKD. Their experiments revealed that when the immune system cannot clear a viral infection, the resulting inflammatory response can cause extensive damage to organs.

These results help explain why a disorder involving defective immune defenses can also produce episodes of extreme inflammation.

Existing Drug Demonstrates Promise for a New Treatment.

The discovery has already helped guide an experimental treatment approach for a severely affected infant.

Working with doctors at the Royal Children's Hospital in Melbourne, the researchers explored whether baricitinib could reduce the excessive inflammatory signaling associated with MKD.

Baricitinib belongs to a class of medications known as JAK inhibitors. These drugs interfere with signaling pathways used by the immune system, including those involved in responses to interferon gamma. The medication is already used to treat other immune-related conditions, including rheumatoid arthritis and eczema.

Doctors added baricitinib to the infant's existing treatment regimen and subsequently observed an improvement in the child's condition. Inflammatory flare-ups became less frequent, and severe inflammation affecting the gastrointestinal tract began to heal.

Although the results from a single patient cannot establish whether the treatment will work more broadly, the improvement provides encouraging early evidence for a strategy that targets a different part of the inflammatory process.

The researchers believe their findings provide a foundation for future clinical studies investigating JAK inhibitors and other medications that block interferon gamma activity in patients with MKD, particularly those who have not benefited from standard treatments.

Discovery Could Help Explain Other Genetic Diseases.

The potential implications extend beyond MKD itself.

Sources indicate that researchers have introduced the term 'prenylopathies' to describe a family of genetic disorders involving the same metabolic pathway affected in MKD. Early findings suggest that these related diseases may share a similar underlying problem involving natural killer cells that fail to function properly and instead generate excessive inflammatory signals.

If further studies confirm this connection, scientists may be able to identify common disease mechanisms and develop more targeted approaches to diagnosis and treatment across multiple disorders.

"Confirming this link could help end the diagnostic odyssey many patients endure for years or even decades before receiving effective treatment," says Professor Rogers.

Professor Mike Rogers is a Conjoint Professor at St Vincent's Clinical School, Faculty of Medicine and Health, UNSW Sydney. Dr. Marcia Munoz is a Conjoint Senior Lecturer at St Vincent's Clinical School, Faculty of Medicine and Health, UNSW Sydney.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Manhattan luxury market has had a banner year despite the pied-à-terre tax and the recent stock market correction.

Trophy properties—those priced $10 million and above—made up half the contracts signed last week, leading the luxury market into the second biggest year in two decades, according to Olshan Realty.

Sources indicate that as of Nov. 22, an impressive 294 contracts were signed at $10 million and above, not far off the peak year of 2021, when 400 were signed. The average asking price for last week was $10.5 million, and properties were moving with a fairly low 5% average discount.

Sources indicate that corcoran's Deborah Grubman, who co-listed last week's most expensive sale—a $28.75 million triplex in the Pritzker Prize–winning Richard Meier building in the West Village—says that the luxury market normally shows signs of slowing down around the Thanksgiving holiday. But not this year.

"New York is still a very desirable destination for people of wealth," she tells Realtor.com®.

The glass triplex at 176 Perry St.—one of the city's most coveted blocks—was owned by Broadway and movie star Hugh Jackman. The condo, built in 2001, had been on and off the market since June 2022, and at one point was priced at $39 million.

Jackman and his ex-wife, Deborra-Lee Furness, purchased the 11,000-square-foot minimalist abode for $21 million in 2008. Spanning the eighth, ninth and 10th floors, it is "one of the most dramatic apartments in Manhattan," the listing states.

According to recent reports, the full-service condominium comes with sweeping views of the river and Hudson River Park and is within walking distance of The High Line, Little Island, the Meatpacking District, Bleecker Steet, and the Whitney Museum. Jean-Georges Vongerichten's Perry Street Restaurant is on its ground floor.

The Richard Meier building, one of the first ultraluxe buildings that far west, helped change the face of the once-gritty area.

"It was the first 'star-chitect' building in the West Village on the waterfront," indicates the broker. "It was groundbreaking in terms of luxury. At the time, people said, 'Who is going to live in the highway?' It predated all that green space.".

While it took Jackman about five years to unload the property, Grubman says that the West Village—and Perry Street, which stretches from Greenwich Avenue to the river—remains in high demand.

"It's a street that's got lots of charm and history," she says. "The West Village is out of central casting. You still have the charm of the small townhouses and tree-lined streets.

"The only thing that's really changed a lot is the price point.".

According to recent reports, michelle Griffith of Douglas Elliman represented the buyer of one of the year's top sales: a $16.5 million, 3,855-square-foot condo in the Waldorf Astoria Residences at 301 Park Ave. in Midtown.

The luxury broker claims her trophy property sales for 2026 are on track to beat her previous best year, which was 2021.

That year, when 400 ultraluxe contracts were signed, those who weren't fleeing lockdowns were shelling out for multimillion-dollar properties, spurred on by historically low interest rates in the 2% to 4% range.

Today, with higher rates hovering around 7%, there are plenty of cash-flush buyers snapping up ultraluxe homes. (Some still prefer 7% mortgage rates to pulling their money out of more lucrative investments.).

According to recent reports, "The phrase that sums up 2026 for me is 'bidding wars,'" the broker tells Realtor.com. "This year will go down as my best year.".

She attributes the surging high-end market to a couple of factors: tight inventory pushing up prices and sparking intense competition, and the "insanely high and insanely competitive" rental market, with rents double or triple what they were just a few years ago.

According to Realtor.com, a three-bedroom-plus in Manhattan has a median monthly rent of $5,375, an increase of 35.6% over the past seven years, requiring a household to earn $215,000 a year just to stay afloat with rent.

In a recent development, however, those who want a luxury three-bedroom-plus abode in a trendy neighborhood can shell out significantly more. Griffith notes that a few years ago, a large luxury dwelling in an area like Tribeca could cost around $19,000 a month. But now?

Recent findings suggest that "It would work itself up close to $30,000," she indicates. "So those people are saying, 'Do I want to spend $30,000 a month or should I pivot and think about buying something? How much am I going to overspend before I say, 'OK, let me buy'?".

Combine stratospheric rents with "inventory levels down across the board," and prices have skyrocketed.

"If you have something good in the West Village, in Tribeca, on the Upper East Side, it is likely going to trade itself up in a bidding war," states the agent.

In a recent development, when dream turnkey apartments began to disappear from listings, buyers became more willing to take on projects, resulting in a stronger-than-normal luxury co-op market. In general, co-ops are much older—and cheaper—than condos.

While the week ending Nov. 22 saw luxury condos outpace co-ops 18-4, there have been several weeks during 2026 when that gap was considerably narrower—and one week in June when co-ops won out.

"These are places that might require several million dollars to renovate," claims Griffith. "And now that market too is getting absorbed.".

She indicates those who didn't leave the city during the COVID-19 pandemic—fleeing to Westchester, Connecticut, or Florida—are the die-hards who are committed to the city long term. And they are the ones out there bidding up and buying.

Especially relevant are families whose children are deep in the school system.

"They're putting down roots for a minimum of 10 to 15 years," she says.

Despite her banner year, Griffith says she isn't planning a celebration just yet. Next year could be a different story as the pied-à-terre surcharge ramps up to replace Department of Finance valuations with significantly higher "fair market" valuations for 2029.

Recent findings suggest that "This year was an emotional journey," she says. "There were many bidding wars we won, but also many we lost. I'm the type who focuses more on, 'What are the deals that we lost?'".

It has been revealed that the second-highest contract of the week was a $25 million sponsor duplex penthouse at 133 E. 73rd St. Listing agency Modlin Group did not return a request for more information.

UPDATED 19:01 EST / NOVEMBER 20 2026.

Sources indicate that president Donald Trump today unveiled aims to impose a “tremendous tax” on U.S. companies that build data centers overseas.

“We’re not allowing data centers to go into other countries because China will take all of them, and we’re not allowing that to happen,” Trump told reporters during a White House briefing.

That hints the blueprint may place particular emphasis on data centers optimized for artificial intelligence workloads. According to recent media reports, Chinese tech firms are using AI-optimized data centers in countries such as Malaysia to train their models. Such deals are designed to bypass U.S. restrictions on the export of advanced AI chips to China.

Industry observers note that if the tax initiative focuses specifically on AI data centers, it’s unclear what facilities would qualify. Cloud providers such as Amazon Web Services Inc. operate international data centers that include a significant number of graphics cards, but also run general-purpose workloads. Some of them were built before the advent of large language models.

Last month, AWS announced prepares to invest 18 billion euros in Germany next year. A part of the capital has been earmarked for data center capacity. A few weeks earlier, Google LLC committed 13 billion euros to building computing infrastructure and supporting assets in Finland. A significant newly introduced tax on international data center projects may lead some industry players to revise their investment plans.

According to recent reports, if Trump’s proposed tax is not focused on AI-optimized data centers alone, it could have even broader implications for cloud providers. He indicated that he did not discuss the strategy with White House officials before announcing it. According to the Associated Press, there’s currently no information on how the tax would be implemented.

Industry observers note that “We want them to build it here. If they won’t go in Texas or they won’t go in California, they’re going to go in West Virginia,” Trump stated. “We have a lot of places that want them badly, and they’re great places.”.

During this month’s midterm elections, voters in multiple states approved ballot measures designed to limit data center construction. On Thursday, a bipartisan group of lawmakers formed a congressional caucus dedicated to tackling AI risks.

Trump’s announcement of the data center tax plan comes a few days after the U.S. Commerce Department imposed new restrictions on overseas AI facilities. The rules are designed to curb Chinese companies’ access to cutting-edge graphics cards.

Recent findings suggest that according to the Financial Times, at least two chipmakers have suspended some hardware shipments in response to the move. Nscale Global Holdings Ltd., a prominent neocloud, will reportedly have to secure a Commerce Department license to continue working with its largest customer.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Will Smith and Jada Pinkett Smith's $42 million Los Angeles property went up in flames after their shed caught fire.
  • The Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department and the Malibu/Lost Hills Sheriff’s Station responded to a 911 call at the property in the early hours of Nov.
  • It has been revealed that officials told People that they arrived to discover a "structure fire" at the couple's Calabasas home.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Will Smith and Jada Pinkett Smith's $42 million Los Angeles property went up in flames after their shed caught fire.

The Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department and the Malibu/Lost Hills Sheriff’s Station responded to a 911 call at the property in the early hours of Nov. 23.

It has been revealed that officials told People that they arrived to discover a "structure fire" at the couple's Calabasas home. They added that no one was hurt.

“It appears a shed caught fire, and the cause is believed to be accidental,” the statement from the sheriff's department revealed.

In audio from the 911 call obtained from Page Six, firefighters can be heard saying, "We do have a shed on fire with no spread to the brush.".

An emergency personnel noted that they were already "on scene," and then another firefighter explained that the fire had been "downgraded to a structure.".

The couple's Calabasas property serves as their primary residence. Set on 150 acres, the estate—which they began working on in 1997, the same year they tied the knot—features high-end amenities, including a basketball court, a tennis court, and a massive swimming pool.

The property was designed by architect Stephen Samuelson, who teamed up with Smith and Pinkett Smith in 1997, after they were inspired by the work he had done on the home of Carol Burnett, according to Architectural Digest.

According to recent reports, however, it was to be a labor of love for the couple—who had to wait four years to secure the permits to begin construction on their dream home. It would sit at the center of an enormous property that they had amassed over time by buying up adjacent plots of land as they became available.

In the end, Smith and Pinkett Smith created an idyllic Mediterranean-inspired sanctuary for their family, boasting all manner of luxury from a meditation lounge and a recording studio to a sunken trampoline.

In a recent development, it was previously believed that Smith and Pinkett Smith were living apart, with the actress revealing during a previous "Today" interview that she had moved into a newly introduced abode in the Los Angeles area. She did not reveal any other details about the property.

The fire comes after Smith, 58, and Pinkett Smith, 55, were spotted in a rare outing alongside their children, Jaden, 28, and Willow, 26.

Last year, the couple put one of their many homes on the market for the relatively low price of $2 million—amid rampant speculation over the state of their marriage.

Many fans have been questioning the status of their relationship since 2022, when Smith infamously slapped Chris Rock across the face during the Oscars ceremony after the comedian made a joke about Pinkett Smith's hair.

Then, just over a year later, Pinkett Smith sensationally revealed during an interview on the "Today" show that she and Smith had been living "completely separate lives" since 2016, despite insisting that they had no plans to legally divorce.

In the two years since that candid confession, questions have continued to be swirl about the truth of their relationship, with Smith sending the rumor mill into overdrive again in February when he put on a very raunchy display with singer India Martínez during an on-stage performance of their song, "First Love.".

Following that public display, the "Men In Black" actor pushed forward a upcoming album, titled "Based on a True Story," marking the first time he has debuted a new record in years.

According to Smith, the album is the result of "self-examination" that began after the Oscars incident, which saw the actor banned from all academy events for 10 years.

"I’ve taken the last couple of years to really do a deep dive on the parts of me that may or may not been in that level of certainty and asking those deep scary internal questions," he told the Associated Press.

According to recent reports, "It really is the result of my initial self-examination. Every song is about some part of myself that I discovered or wanted to explore, something I wanted to share. It’s the most full musical offering that I’ve ever created.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • AI operational readiness requires more than selecting the right servers, storage and computing capacity.
  • It has been revealed that those considerations are particularly consequential for financial institutions, where reliability, regulatory obligations and the need to demonstrate returns on technology investments shape deployment decisions.
  • Recent findings suggest that “I think the pyramid still exists, but undoubtedly, the cost of entry and the barriers to entry have crumbled,” he told theCUBE.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 19:21 EST / NOVEMBER 20 2026.

AI operational readiness requires more than selecting the right servers, storage and computing capacity.

It has been revealed that those considerations are particularly consequential for financial institutions, where reliability, regulatory obligations and the need to demonstrate returns on technology investments shape deployment decisions. Meanwhile, AI is changing the threat landscape, giving less sophisticated attackers access to capabilities that once required considerably greater resources, according to John Scimone, president and chief security officer of Dell Technologies Inc.

Recent findings suggest that “I think the pyramid still exists, but undoubtedly, the cost of entry and the barriers to entry have crumbled,” he told theCUBE. “Said another way, the least sophisticated attack tomorrow is more sophisticated than the world will have ever seen a year ago.”.

Scimone spoke with theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante during the Dell Technologies Fresh York Symposium, part of SiliconANGLE Media’s exclusive coverage on theCUBE. Across the event, Dell executives and cloud infrastructure providers examined the economics of enterprise AI, the operational challenges of scaling infrastructure and the decisions shaping AI adoption.

Here is theCUBE’s complete video discussion with John Scimone:.

Here are three insights you might have missed from theCUBE’s coverage of the Dell Technologies New York Symposium:.

In a recent development, dell has spent nearly two years running fully autonomous agents internally, capturing institutional knowledge in machine-readable skill files that guide their behavior. The effort is part of a broader reorganization of work around AI agents, according to John Roese, global chief technology officer and chief AI officer of Dell.

According to recent reports, “It doesn’t mean you can’t use frontier models and open models,” he said during the event. “It just means that when you design your AI system, you need to realize that the thing that is your moat is not the actual tools. It’s not even the models. It’s the special knowledge that’s now manifesting in these upcoming forms that really capture what you know and do differently than your competitors.”.

Here is theCUBE’s complete video discussion with John Roese:.

The financial side of AI operational readiness presents a different challenge. As enterprises scale their deployments, finance teams are establishing dedicated budget lines for token consumption and evaluating which workloads can run more economically on-premises. Repetitive financial processes, for example, can use open-weight models to convert variable token expenses into more predictable fixed costs, according to David Kennedy, chief financial officer of Dell.

“It’s not necessarily about the amount and the cost of a token,” he told theCUBE. “It’s about the tokens you use. Can you be efficient with them? If you are, you’re going to see great outcomes.”.

Here is theCUBE’s complete video discussion with David Kennedy:.

The growth of AI inference is changing how enterprises distribute workloads across cloud environments, data centers and edge devices. Dell’s expanded agentic AI portfolio reflects that shift, with solutions spanning desktop systems and data center infrastructure. Organizations are evaluating where to run models based on performance, data control and cost, according to Kyle Dufresne, senior vice president of sales at Dell.

“We’re seeing the business owners saying, ‘Oh my gosh, these costs are getting really high for inferencing. How do we reduce those costs without curbing innovation?’” he said during the event. “We’re finding it’s happening across that continuum but more and more right out at the far edge.”.

Here is theCUBE’s complete video discussion with Kyle Dufresne:.

According to recent reports, infrastructure availability presents another challenge. Demand for AI servers has strained supplies of components ranging from memory and processors to rack-level cooling, networking and power equipment, according to David Schmoock, senior vice president of global revenue operations at Dell.

Recent findings suggest that “We didn’t do that collaborative planning, and now your project may have been delayed 60, 90, 120 days, which has both the cost impact and a business impact,” he told theCUBE. “I would say bring us in earlier. Allow us to do that collaboration with you. I think, at the end of the day, you get the most optimal outcome.”.

Here is theCUBE’s complete video discussion with David Schmoock:.

According to recent reports, AI operational readiness is also becoming a consideration for smaller businesses that need access to GPU computing without the resources of large enterprises. Comet Cloud Inc. is targeting this underserved market, where access to AI infrastructure can be constrained by purchasing commitments and provider priorities, according to Thomas Kato, founder and chief executive officer of Comet Cloud.

Industry observers note that “You go to [Amazon Web Services] now; they want a multiyear contract from you. They’re picking who they’re taking,” he said during the event. “To the small and medium businesses, they’re not even coming up on that scope at all to be able to have that AI. Really, that’s our focus.”.

Comet Cloud is developing an alternative approach aimed at giving smaller organizations greater control over their computing environments, Kato noted.

“What we do is we put together clusters, and we’re giving clusters to a whole company. All their information, all their security, everything is within that cluster. There’s no one else tied or connected to it,” he told theCUBE.

Here’s theCUBE’s complete video discussion with Thomas Kato:.

Alpha Compute Corp. is also building its neocloud infrastructure around data sovereignty and confidential computing requirements. The company’s sovereign-by-design approach is intended to help customers maintain control over sensitive workloads and meet data residency obligations, including those associated with European regulations, according to Tom Richer, executive vice president of Alpha Compute.

“We start with the hardware. Think of a stack. All the way down to the chip level, we are creating enclaves,” he told theCUBE. “We’re a Dell partner, so we use Dell technology as well as Intel technology.”.

Industry observers note that keeping GPU infrastructure operational presents a different challenge for neocloud providers. Alpha Compute provides integrated infrastructure support and ongoing managed services to address those demands, Richer noted.

“You can cobble together a lot of different providers, but then when stuff goes wrong, the finger-pointing starts,” he remarked during the event. “You just want that integrated solution provider who can ensure success, help you with all of the build-out, then all of the … managed services to keep it going healthy and to keep everything performing in line with [service-level agreements].”.

Here is theCUBE’s complete video discussion with Tom Richer:.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Binance founder Changpeng Zhao, widely known as CZ, has expressed his concerns about the storage of sensitive personal data after Japanese authorities called on rental car services to delete customers' identity documents following a massive data breach.
  • In a recent development, in his latest X post, CZ pointed to a Nov.
  • The recent call by Japanese authorities comes after a massive cybersecurity attack on a popular Japanese car-sharing service called Times Car, operated by Park24 Group.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Binance founder Changpeng Zhao, widely known as CZ, has expressed his concerns about the storage of sensitive personal data after Japanese authorities called on rental car services to delete customers' identity documents following a massive data breach.

In a recent development, in his latest X post, CZ pointed to a Nov. 18 notice issued by Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission (PPC). The notice urges rental car services to be cautious about unnecessarily storing images of driver’s licenses and other government-issued identification documents.

The recent call by Japanese authorities comes after a massive cybersecurity attack on a popular Japanese car-sharing service called Times Car, operated by Park24 Group.

The incident began when the manufacturer noticed suspicious activity on its system on Sept. 25. As a result, it rolled out an investigation into whether someone had accessed its systems without permission, potentially exposing customer data.

As per the disclosure by Park24 on Oct. 23, about 6.63 million customer accounts were impacted by the breach.

Worse, the investigation uncovered evidence that hackers had transmitted 1,464,800 encrypted images of identification documents, including driver’s licenses, to external locations.

Besides that, another 891,602 encrypted images of identification documents were accessed suspiciously. However, investigators found no evidence that these additional ID images had been transmitted outside the organization’s systems.

According to recent reports, japan’s Personal Information Protection Commission issued its notice on Nov. 18, focusing on the risks of retaining sensitive personal data even after its original purpose has been fulfilled.

The regulatory body stressed that storing unnecessary identification images could significantly worsen the consequences of cyberattacks.

Although Japan’s latest warning specifically targets the rental car industry, CZ’s decision to share his concerns about this issue also raises questions about personal data protection in the crypto industry.

Generally, centralized crypto exchanges require users to go through a Know Your Customer (KYC) process to access their trading platforms.

Depending on the platform and jurisdiction, these processes may require users to provide photos of their passports, driver’s licenses, national ID cards, and other sensitive information.

This kind of sensitive data can be a goldmine for cybercriminals, who can exploit stolen personal information for various activities such as identity theft, phishing attacks, fraudulent registrations, and more.

Why an Uninsulated Garage Can Wreak Havoc on Your Home This Winter

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (566 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Realtor

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • An uninsulated garage might seem like no big deal, but come the winter months, it can do more harm than good.
  • In fact, when a garage lacks proper insulation during the colder months, frozen pipes, heat loss, and damaged items are bound to arise.
  • Fortunately, insulation solutions and preventive measures can help you avoid these concerns while protecting your garage, your car, and your home.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An uninsulated garage might seem like no big deal, but come the winter months, it can do more harm than good.

In fact, when a garage lacks proper insulation during the colder months, frozen pipes, heat loss, and damaged items are bound to arise.

Fortunately, insulation solutions and preventive measures can help you avoid these concerns while protecting your garage, your car, and your home.

An uninsulated garage in the winter months can cause a chain reaction of concerns to the home itself. One of the most common risks is frozen pipes.

“When the plumbing or water lines located in the garage get exposed to below-freezing temps, they may freeze and cause water damage,” explains Chris Boyle, in-house repair tech at Parts Town Home and Fix.com in Nova Scotia.

Additionally, improperly insulated garages can prompt heat loss throughout the entire home.

“Many poorly insulated garages share foundations with homes. As a result, cold air may circulate through the living spaces and force families to turn up their heating systems,” claims Boyle.

Not only does this put a strain on HVAC systems, it can also drive up monthly heating bills.

Plus, poor insulation may damage items stored in the garage, particularly car batteries, which can lose charge or fail completely.

So, how do you know for sure whether your garage is insulated?

On a cold day, compare the temperature inside your garage to the outside.

If your garage feels as cold as the outdoors, or if the rooms adjacent to it are always noticeably colder in the winter, there’s a good chance it’s not insulated.

Sources indicate that “You can also inspect the walls and ceiling for visible insulation. On the garage door, thin or hollow panels usually indicate a lack of insulation, while thicker panels often mean insulating material is present,” explains Paul Sharpe, owner at Surfside Garage Doors in Toms River, NJ.

Once you determine you have an uninsulated garage, here are several tips to keep on your radar.

For a faster, practical insulation solution, seal any of the bottom gaps under your garage door with rubber weatherstripping.

“If your budget and resources allow, however, the most effective way to retain heat in your garage is to insulate all the walls with fiberglass insulation,” states Chris Hunter, director of customer relations at ServiceTitan in Glendale, CA.

Regardless of your choice, these solutions will help decrease your energy bill and create a more comfortable environment.

It has been revealed that since the garage door is the largest opening in your home, investing in an insulated garage door may be worthwhile. Entry-level insulated doors typically provide an R-value between 6 and 9, while higher-end models can reach R-values of around 20.

“The higher the R-value, the higher the insulation capabilities and less heat loss that will occur,” explains Sharpe.

You don’t have to expose your valuables to the risks of an uninsulated garage.

“To avoid damaging your items in the garage during winter, you may either elevate them or bring them inside your insulated home,” states Tamer Sayed, licensed HVAC technician and the owner-operator of Tamas Mechanical in Mississauga, Ontario.

In a recent development, before the winter begins (or even after, if you missed the boat), consult an HVAC professional for an insulation evaluation. The pro can determine whether your garage is properly safeguarded for the season and recommend the best next steps.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 20:50 EST / NOVEMBER 20 2026.

CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. is reportedly in talks to buy Zscaler Inc., a publicly traded provider of cybersecurity software.

Sources told Bloomberg today that the acquisition could “come together soon.” However, they cautioned that it’s still possible the talks will fall through.

According to recent reports, investors seem to be confident that the deal will materialize. Zscaler’s share price jumped more than 16% in after-hours trading, while CrowdStrike dropped about 4.8%.

Software buyouts tend to value the acquired company at a premium to its last unaffected market capitalization. As a result, CrowdStrike is likely to pay more than the $32 billion Zscaler was worth at the end of today’s trading session. That means the deal could take CrowdStrike’s market capitalization above $250 billion.

It has been revealed that crowdStrike sells one of the world’s most popular cybersecurity platforms. Falcon can detect and block malicious activity across cloud instances, on-premises servers, employee devices and other assets. It also automates certain related tasks, such as finding sensitive records that are stored in an insecure manner.

In a recent development, zscaler competes in a different part of the cybersecurity market. It sells software that protects the network connections through which a firm’s employees access its business applications.

Enterprises historically used virtual private network, or VPN, tools for that task. Such programs tend to be quite slow. More significantly, they give employees access to the entire corporate network rather than to the specific applications they need for their work. That broad access can create cybersecurity risks.

In a recent development, zscaler sells a zero-trust network access, or ZTNA, platform designed to replace legacy VPN software. It limits the number of applications that workers can access within the corporate network. If Zscaler detects risky activity, it asks the affected user to complete additional authentication steps.

The tech giant’s ZTNA software doubles as an observability tool. Administrators can monitor employees’ connections for technical challenges that may hinder productivity. A built-in artificial intelligence assistant, the ZDX Agent, generates troubleshooting advice.

Zscaler also competes in other product categories where CrowdStrike has a limited presence. Notably, it offers a tool that deploys bogus applications, user passwords and files in customer networks. Those simulated assets act as sensors. When an attempt is made to access one of them, Zscaler Deception notifies the customer that a cyberattack is underway.

The potential deal would mark CrowdStrike’s largest acquisition by a wide margin. The manufacturer’s biggest buyout to date is its $970 million purchase of startup SGNL Inc., which closed earlier this year. The deal bought CrowdStrike a platform that can automatically end users’ application sessions when it detects cybersecurity problems.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • XRP stands out as the cryptocurrency with the most alarming volatility warning among major digital assets, according to recent Coinbase data.
  • XRP's seven-day options-implied price move stands at 1.94 times its historical median.
  • XRP exhibits the highest premium above its own historical volatility.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

XRP stands out as the cryptocurrency with the most alarming volatility warning among major digital assets, according to recent Coinbase data. The options market indicates that traders are now preparing for price swings that could be nearly double XRP's historical seven-day price move.

XRP's seven-day options-implied price move stands at 1.94 times its historical median. This figure far exceeds similar metrics for major cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH) and Solana (SOL).

XRP exhibits the highest premium above its own historical volatility. Solana demonstrates the lowest premium among these four cryptocurrencies, Coinbase remarked.

Recent findings suggest that as the chart below indicates, the options-implied seven-day price move for XRP is around 9.6%, according to Glassnode and Coinbase data as of Nov. 17. This compares to its historical median absolute price move of about 4.9%.

Basically, this means that the options market is signaling a price swing nearly twice as large as XRP's typical seven-day price movement.

Industry observers note that interestingly, Solana's implied price move is also close to 9.5%, almost the same as XRP's. Yet its historical median weekly price move is much higher at about 6.5%.

The key here is that although both cryptocurrencies exhibit similarly large potential price moves, the magnitude of the expected volatility surprise is significantly greater for XRP relative to its usual trading range.

It has been revealed that for comparison, Bitcoin shows an options-implied seven-day move of about 6%, versus its historical median of about 3.5%. For Ethereum, these numbers are about 8% and 5.1%, respectively.

Sources indicate that obviously, this latest figure doesn't necessarily imply that XRP is going to crash. It's a sign that options traders expect a big price move regardless of its direction.

Implied volatility is a forward-looking measure. It's based on options prices. The higher the implied volatility, the more traders pay for exposure to potential price movements or protection against them.

The chart from Coinbase is based on a one-standard-deviation estimate. It's derived by converting annualized at-the-money implied volatility into a seven-day timeframe.

For XRP, the roughly 9.6% implied move represents a statistical range. It's not a guaranteed price target. A one-standard-deviation range suggests about a 68% chance of the price staying within this range under typical modeling assumptions.

Thus, the latest figure of 1.94x implies that XRP's volatility premium remains high despite a slight decrease from the previous reading.

From XRP traders' perspective, this can be a very challenging market environment. For traders using leverage, there could be a high risk of liquidation due to potentially sharp price moves.

#167872. Buying a Home Soon? This Overlooked Open Enrollment Perk Could Save You Thousands in Legal Fees
